name: Center of Contemporary Art Tbilisi (Tbilisi Triennial)
funding: A small independent non-profit and organiser of the Tbilisi Triennial, funded by foreign governments and foundations (Swiss SDC, German Foreign Office, Danish funds) and individual donors.
watch: Founded by Wato Tsereteli in 2010. Nearly all its funding is foreign, so Georgia's 2025 foreign-agents law exposes it.
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; the supporters page names nine key benefactors and individual donors with no date; no board is listed.

name: National Gallery of Armenia
funding: A state gallery on Republic Square, founded in 1921 and run under Armenia's Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports; its budget and sponsors were not found.
watch: Armenia's largest art collection, about 42,000 works.
records_note: The gallery's site carries no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; it lists branches, collection, visits and education only.

name: Baku Museum of Modern Art
funding: Opened 20 Mar 2009 with about 800 works; founded by First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva and funded by the Heydar Aliyev Foundation, which she heads.
watch: A ruling-family foundation is its only known funder; the director since 2012 is Aida Mahmudova, founder of YARAT.
records_note: The museum's site, live copy down, shows no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; it carries only about, visit, library and what's-on pages.

name: National Museum of the Republic of Kazakhstan
watch: Aug-Sep 2026 show co-organised with sanctioned oligarch Vladimir Potanin's Olympic Collection.
records_note: The museum's site posts legal acts and anti-corruption pages but no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: State Museum of Arts of Uzbekistan
funding: A state museum founded in 1918 with over 100,000 objects; a new Tadao Ando building is commissioned by the state ACDF, broke ground 27 Aug 2025 and is due in Mar 2028.
watch: Its rebuild is run by the same state foundation as the Bukhara Biennial, whose lead partners include Bukhara Oil.
records_note: The museum and its renovation sponsor, the Art and Culture Development Foundation, publish no reports, accounts or funder list, and name only a chairperson.

name: FESPACO
funding: About 1.3-1.5bn FCFA executed in 2025 (~US$2.3M), nearly 80% from the Burkina state; EU 195M FCFA, plus the UN, OIF, LONAB lottery and telecoms.
watch: Pan-African film festival, held every two years since 1969. The 2025 edition was nearly 80% state-funded under the military transition.
records_note: No reports, accounts or board posted; partners and media partners blocks show undated logos, and the sponsor slot shows the organiser's logo.

name: Lagos Biennial
funding: Small artist-run biennial (2024 edition; 2026 announced) by Àkéte Art Foundation; funded by Terra, Ford and Rockefeller Brothers Fund.
watch: Artist-founded biennial led by Folakunle Oshun. Its 4th edition, 2024, ran in Tafawa Balewa Square.
records_note: No reports or accounts found; the supporters page shows about 40 logos, mostly without alt text, and the site names six advisory board members.

name: Musée National Boubou Hama
funding: State museum of Niger, about 170k visitors (2013); government-funded, with a planned Museum of the River backed by the University of Chicago and private donors.
watch: Niger's national museum since 1959, with a zoo and the Arbre du Ténéré. Its uranium pavilion was historically built with Cogema.
records_note: No official site was found for this national museum, and nothing from it or its ministry on reports, accounts, donors or board.

name: Kin ArtStudio
funding: Small artist-run residency (active 2024); housed in the TEXAF concession, with Pro Helvetia residencies and Fondation Montresso partnership.
watch: Residency and studio founded 2011 by Vitshois Mwilambwe Bondo in a former TEXAF textile hangar. Linked to the Congo Biennale.
records_note: No Kin ArtStudio site could be opened; one interview names only Fondation Montresso as partner, and the founder funds it from art sales.

name: Musée National du Cameroun
funding: State museum under the Ministry of Arts and Culture; €1M modernisation from AFD via debt-swap C2D (2019-24), Phase 2 2025-27, run by Expertise France.
watch: National museum in the former presidential palace since 1988. Its modernisation is funded by French debt conversion.
records_note: It has no site of its own found and publishes no reports, accounts, funder list or board; its funders appear only on AFD project pages.

name: Chale Wote Street Art Festival
funding: Free street festival (15th edition Aug 2025) by ACCRA [dot] ALT; 2023 supported by Ghana's tourism ministry, Ghana Tourism Authority, Citi FM, Institut Français.
watch: Accra's street art festival, held in Jamestown since 2011. The Ghana Tourism Authority helped keep the 2023 edition going.
records_note: The organiser's site posts no reports, accounts or board, and names supporters only inside festival announcements, not on a standing funder page.

name: Le 32Bis
funding: Private initiative opened Feb 2022 in the former Philips HQ; funded by Tunisian private patrons who are not named; partners include the African Culture Fund.
watch: 4,000 m² centre with residencies, exhibitions and a library in downtown Tunis; opened Feb 2022.
records_note: 32bis.org lists no annual reports, accounts, partners, funders, board or team.
